front: σ and π in single, double and triple bonds?
sp³, sp², sp: shapes and angles?
back: sp³: tetrahedral, 109.5°. sp²: trigonal planar, 120°. sp: linear, 180°.

front: Why is a π bond weaker than a σ bond?
back: Sideways overlap of p orbitals is less effective than end-on overlap.

front: Why is rotation about C=C restricted?
back: Rotation would twist the p orbitals out of line and break the π bond.
The sp² σ framework is planar, and the two p orbitals forming the π bond must be parallel.
Each C is sp² with three σ bonds; the six leftover p orbitals overlap to form a delocalised π system above and below the ring.
